Record Class BehaviorKey<V>

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.trevlar.slotkit.api.window.BehaviorKey<V>
Record Components:
id - the stable name.
valueType - the resolved value's type, for type-safe storage.
libraryDefault - the bottom of the cascade, a neutral value that matches vanilla, returned when nothing overrides. It is why resolve never returns null.
tier - Tier.CLIENT (works on any server) or Tier.SERVER (needs SlotKit on the server).
appliesTo - which KindTags this behavior is valid on, checked at the call boundary (a slot verb is unreachable on a panel), never inside resolution.
public record BehaviorKey<V>(net.minecraft.resources.Identifier id, Class<V> valueType, V libraryDefault, Tier tier, EnumSet<KindTag> appliesTo) extends Record
Names one behavior the window can resolve: gating, visibility, a panel's opacity, a reaction and so on. The engine is generic over the key, so adding a behavior means declaring a new BehaviorKey (id, value type, library default, tier, applicable kinds), with no engine change.
